Messages.Author: DJ.Mik
Messages.Body:
Combat:

Minion A plays S:CE
Minion B strikes with Ivory bow

Minion B wants to play Rotschreck on minion A, but minion A plays
Mayaparisitia at inferior.

What happens ?

A. Minion A goes to torpor with Rotschreck ?

or

B. Combat ends since Ivory bow no longer inflicts any damage ?

I'd say B, but I promsed to ask because we've discussed it in our
playgroup this evening.

Thanks in advance
DJ Mik

Minion A cannot play Mayaparisatya *after* a rotschreck is declared. So
Rotschreck immediatly takes effect, like all master cards, and A goes to
torpor tapped with the card on him.

If meh A knew that B had a Rotschreck in hand (owl companion, aura reading)
he could have played it before B played Rotschreck to prevent it from being
played.

Messages.Author: Gregory Stuart Pettigrew
Messages.Body:
> Combat:
>
> Minion A plays S:CE
> Minion B strikes with Ivory bow
>
> Minion B wants to play Rotschreck on minion A, but minion A plays
> Mayaparisitia at inferior.
>

Let's assume Minion A is acting. This isn't too crazy an assumption since
Minion B's controller wants to play an OOT Master.

Minion A's controller gets to play cards first. If he chooses to play
Mayaparisatya, then Minion B's controller is SOL. Now, he played S:CE, so
he's probably not going to bother with the Mayaparisatya.

> What happens ?
>
> A. Minion A goes to torpor with Rotschreck ?
>
> or
>
> B. Combat ends since Ivory bow no longer inflicts any damage ?
>
> I'd say B, but I promsed to ask because we've discussed it in our
> playgroup this evening.
>

Minion B's controller should ask if Minion A's controller wishes to play
anything else before strikes resolve. A simple "Is that it?" should be
sufficient. After he has chosen to play no further cards, Minion B's
controller can play the Rotschreck and it is then too late to play
Mayaparisatya.

Messages.Author: Gregory Stuart Pettigrew
Messages.Body:
> Of course there is the window. A has alaways a chance to interrupt card
> flow.

That is not true. The acting minion does not get an opportunity to play a
card in between the time you grab the card out of your hand and you show
it to everybody, or between the time you show it to everybody and declare
its effects.

The acting minion has the option of playing between the Ivory Bow and the
Rotschreck, and MUST DECLARE, directly or not, that he is not playing
anything in that window. Simply asking "Is that it then?" from B to A
should be sufficient.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Gregory Stuart Pettigrew wrote:

>>Of course there is the window. A has alaways a chance to interrupt card
>>flow.
>
> That is not true. The acting minion does not get an opportunity to play a
> card in between the time you grab the card out of your hand and you show
> it to everybody, or between the time you show it to everybody and declare
> its effects.

Splitting hairs. There is no time "between" the things you mention, at
least as far as the rules are concerned. The acting minion always has
a chance to interrupt card flow by playing the next effect.

> The acting minion has the option of playing between the Ivory Bow and the
> Rotschreck, and MUST DECLARE, directly or not, that he is not playing
> anything in that window. Simply asking "Is that it then?" from B to A
> should be sufficient.

B needn't ask, though. A is in control of the clock - the onus is on him
if on anyone. He should directly declare that he is no playing anything
or make it known to the other players' satisfaction (by the appropriate
pause) or be prepared to back up if he "skips" ahead to the strike
resolution (damage prevention, damage handling, etc.)

It may take some prompting from the B's of the world to get the A's
into the habit, but it's a good habit to get into.
